answer: The routing module predicts boundaries between adjacent elements using a similarity score [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2] and dynamically draws chunk boundaries [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 3, §1 −'!"$]. The smoothing module interpolates representations using the router’s outputs to convert discrete chunks into interpolated representations, which attenuates the effect of uncertain boundaries and improves learnability by addressing the discrete nature of chunk boundaries that impedes gradient flow [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2][Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 6, §2.2.2 Dechunking][Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 3, §1 −'!"$]. The auxiliary loss function targets desired downsampling ratios [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2].
question: Dynamic chunking has to pick boundaries and still train with ordinary gradients. What do the routing module and the smoothing module each do, and what is the auxiliary loss for?
raw_answer: The routing module predicts boundaries between adjacent elements using a similarity score [[cite:4eca1e440cbe6544]] and dynamically draws chunk boundaries [[cite:03fadd79e501ecb2]]. The smoothing module interpolates representations using the router’s outputs to convert discrete chunks into interpolated representations, which attenuates the effect of uncertain boundaries and improves learnability by addressing the discrete nature of chunk boundaries that impedes gradient flow [[cite:4eca1e440cbe6544]][[cite:a70741935f0c7653]][[cite:03fadd79e501ecb2]]. The auxiliary loss function targets desired downsampling ratios [[cite:4eca1e440cbe6544]].
